deep.reconstruction:
This is a programme or to-do page for the continuation of 'Pursuing Stacks' (1983), headed 'Asphéricité'. Grothendieck lists open questions in the theory of modelizers (categories whose localization by weak equivalences models homotopy types):
(1) What is a morphism of asphericity structures, and how do inverse images work? An asphericity structure on a category M is a class of 'aspherical' objects or maps with stability properties, used to define weak equivalences without passing through Cat.
(2) What are contractors (categories of contractible objects used to build canonical modelizers), and what are morphisms between them?
(3) Induced asphericity structures on slice categories M/a, marked for part VI.
(4) 'Lack of contractibility', i.e. situations where aspherical objects need not be contractible.
(5) When does an asphericity structure (or a 'structure type') give rise to a canonical modelizer? Marked 'V ? Also VII'.
(6) Existence theorems for test functors A -> M. This item is crossed out.
(7) Finiteness conditions in an elementary modelizer (presheaves on a test category). Crossed out or merged with 6, as the arrow indicates.
(8) Computation of homology by a boundary operator, i.e. a chain-complex description of the abelianization (homology) for presheaves on a test category, generalizing the simplicial Moore complex.
(9) Δ^f and 'infinitesimal' and finite simplicial submodelizers of (Cat). The idea is to find small full subcategories of Cat, for example finite nerves or posets, that are themselves modelizers.
The closing note triages the list: 7 and 8 may not be treated at all; 2, 3 and 9 belong in part IV; 1, 4, 5 and 6 can come later. The next page continues the inventory of candidate test categories: Δ^f, □, □^f, the globular ○ and ○^f, B_f(I), and asphericity or contractibility structures on (Ord). It also asks whether total 0-connectedness implies total asphericity.
The page serves to organize the material of Pursuing Stacks on test categories, asphericity structures, contractors and canonical modelizers.
errors: No mathematical assertions are made, only questions, so there is nothing to be wrong.
The roman numerals (IV, V, VI, VII) refer to Grothendieck's planned parts. These may not match the final chapter division of Pursuing Stacks.
